Henrik Saalbach | Universität Leipzig
Julia Kerner auch Koerner | Universität Münster

Die Selbstregulationsfähigkeit unterliegt im Kindergartenalter einer ausgeprägten Entwicklungsdynamik (Pauen, 2016). Zentrale Komponenten dieser Entwicklung, insbesondere die Fähigkeit zum Aufschub unmittelbarer Impulse sowie das flexible Wechseln zwischen Aufgabenanforderungen, werden den exekutiven Funktionen zugeschrieben. Gut ausgeprägte exekutive Funktionen sind mit höherer Schulreife, höheren schulischen Leistungen und einer besseren psychischen Gesundheit (Bierman et al., 2002) assoziiert. Im deutschsprachigen Raum ist eine standardisierte und umfassende Erfassung im Kindergartenalter bislang nur eingeschränkt möglich, da normierte Testinstrumente fehlen. Ziel der vorliegenden Studie war die Evaluation und Normierung der computergestützten Testbatterie EF Touch (Willoughby & Blair, 2015) für deutschsprachige Kinder im Kindergartenalter. Die Datenerhebung der repräsentativen Gesamtstichprobe umfasste 434 Kinder (218 Mädchen; M = 4,10 Jahre, SD = 0,87) im Alter von 3;0 bis 5;11 Jahren und wurde im April 2023 abgeschlossen. Die Kinder bearbeiteten in zwei Testdurchgängen acht Aufgaben der EF Touch-Batterie sowie ergänzende Validierungsverfahren. Zusätzlich erfolgte eine elterliche Einschätzung mittels standardisierter Fragebögen. Ergebnisse der Konstruktionsstichprobe (n = 90) liegen bereits publiziert vor (Ulitzka et al., 2023). Die psychometrische Prüfung ergab überwiegend akzeptable bis sehr gute interne Konsistenzen (α = .62–.93) sowie signifikante Interkorrelationen zwischen den Aufgaben (r = .14–.42). Altersabhängige Leistungszuwächse zeigten sich über alle Aufgaben hinweg, Geschlechtsunterschiede gab es nicht. Darüber hinaus zeigten sich signifikante Zusammenhänge mit elterlichen Einschätzungen der exekutiven Dysfunktionen (BRIEF-P, r = −.21), Verhaltensauffälligkeiten (SDQ, r = −.26) sowie mit der HTKS-Aufgabe (r = .37–.42). Insgesamt sprechen die Befunde für zufriedenstellende Gütekriterien und belegen die Eignung der adaptierten EF-Touch-Testbatterie zur Erfassung exekutiver Funktionen im Kindergartenalter im deutschsprachigen Raum.

399. Cooperation in STEM and Non-STEM University Courses: Mindsets and Networks
Prof. Lysann Zander | Leibniz Universitaet Hannover | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Prof. Lysann Zander | Leibniz Universitaet Hannover | Germany
Elisabeth Höhne | Leibniz Universität Hannover
Prof. Dr. Kevin Binning | University of Pittsburgh
Prof. Dr. Gregory D. Webster | University of Florida - Gainesville, FL

Cooperation is central to learning in higher education, yet the beliefs and contextual norms that support it vary across fields (Johnson, Johnson, & Smith, 2007). We introduce cooperative mindsets, that is, beliefs that cooperation promotes academic success, and report (a) a validated scale, (b) associations with help-seeking and engagement across gender-typed fields, and (c) a pilot intervention designed to make cooperation visible and normative. Across three studies (N = 1,156), the 10-item Cooperative and Competitive Mindset Scale (CoCoM) showed a robust two-factor structure (cooperative vs. competitive), measurement invariance across STEM and non-STEM fields, and satisfactory reliability and validity. In a separate study (N = 590), cooperative mindsets predicted higher engagement, mediated by more autonomy-oriented help-seeking and lower avoidance. Women reported stronger cooperative mindsets; unexpectedly, STEM students scored higher on cooperative mindsets than HEED students, while competitive mindsets varied less consistently. However, independent network mapping of cooperation ties (N = 435) revealed substantially sparser cooperation networks in STEM than in HEED classes. This pattern suggests a mindset–context gap consistent with pluralistic ignorance: students may perceive cooperation as beneficial while underestimating how much their peers endorse it. Finally, we pilot a cluster-randomized field experiment with a delayed intervention in first-year tutorials (current N ≈ 600). Sessions communicate a cooperation norm, provide structured cooperative practice, and include a brief reflection plus a late-semester booster, with instructors as implementation partners. All studies were conducted with higher-education students in Germany across multiple fields (total N = 2,181 excluding the ongoing pilot study).

400. Sequential (vs. simultaneous) dating profile presentation increases choice satisfaction, but also FOMO, and decision fatigue
Dr. Marina F. Thomas | Karl Landsteiner University of Health Sciences | Austria
Show details
Authors:
Jessica De La Mare | University of Stirling
Dr. Marina F. Thomas | Karl Landsteiner University of Health Sciences | Austria

The way options are presented can shape decision-making, with sequential and simultaneous formats influencing cognitive and emotional outcomes differently. Much previous research focuses on consumer decision-making or witness identification. Traditional dating websites often present profiles simultaneously on a single page, whereas modern dating apps, which are now more commonly used, mostly present profiles sequentially such that each profile must be evaluated before the next is shown. The current preregistered experiment (https://aspredicted.org/gjkp-7fkc.pdf) extends prior work by investigating the effect of dating profile presentation format (simultaneous vs sequential) on several cognitive and emotional outcomes.
Participants (N = 117, M age = 22.37 years, SD age = 2.22 years) evaluated either 21 male or female dating profiles (accept or reject) and completed questionnaires measuring their partner choice overload, decision satisfaction, partner choice FOMO, decision fatigue, self-efficacy, and commodification beliefs. Results indicate that sequential profile presentation was associated with greater decision satisfaction, partner choice FOMO, and decision fatigue than simultaneous presentation. Profile presentation format was not found to significantly affect partner choice overload, self-efficacy, or commodification beliefs.
These findings suggest that swiping on dating apps that present dating profiles sequentially may be associated with detrimental cognitive and emotional outcomes, despite participants reporting increased decision satisfaction. Given the widespread use of such dating apps, identifying platform design features that influence user experience is crucial.

401. The Desire for Greater Antagonism: Psychopathic Traits, Change Goals, and Antisocial Behavior in Non-Forensic Men
Maximilian F. Schwarz | FernUniversitaet in Hagen | Germany
Show details
Author:
Maximilian F. Schwarz | FernUniversitaet in Hagen | Germany

Background. Psychopathic traits affect 5-10% of community adults and are linked to violence, substance misuse, and occupational deviance. Phillips et al.'s (2025) meta-analysis (k = 50) established the Elemental Psychopathy Assessment's nomological net, confirming EPA associations with externalizing outcomes. However, intimate partner violence (including cyber-IPV) and counterproductive work behavior remain untested for the EPA-SF, and no study has examined whether volitional change goals mediate trait-behavior associations.
Methods. A community sample (N = 509 males) completed the EPA-SF, a new EPA Change Goals Inventory (two factors: Impulsive Antagonism, Social Agency), and validated measures of intimate partner violence (face-to-face and cyber), counterproductive work behavior, substance use, and antisocial behavior. ESEM-within-CFA established the measurement model; Structural-After-Measurement estimation was applied for structural paths. Storey's false discovery rate correction controlled for multiple comparisons; indirect effects used BCa bootstrap confidence intervals (5,000 replications).
Results. EPA-SF dimensions showed differential prediction: Antagonism uniquely predicted cyber-IPV; Narcissism was the strongest predictor of counterproductive work behavior; Disinhibition predicted alcohol use; and both Antagonism and Narcissism predicted general antisocial behavior. Emotional Stability showed no significant direct effects, supporting its peripheral role in psychopathy. Critically, Antagonism predicted desire for more antagonistic traits (ego-syntonic), whereas Disinhibition predicted desire for fewer such traits (ego-dystonic). Change goals largely failed to mediate trait-behavior associations, with only two indirect pathways reaching significance.
Conclusions. Extending meta-analytic evidence, subclinical psychopathic traits predict domain-specific antisocial outcomes in community samples. The ego-syntonic valuation of antagonism represents a structural barrier to volitional personality change, with implications for therapeutic engagement beyond forensic settings.

402. Trust the police? Der Einfluss von Status und Uniform auf die Wahrnehmung der Glaubwürdigkeit von Zeug:innen
Dr. Ulrike Stühler | Marburg University | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Dr. Ulrike Stühler | Marburg University | Germany
Pauline S. Moran | Marburg University | Germany
Prof. Dr. Kristina Suchotzki | Germany

Zeug:innenaussagen stellen das am häufigsten herangezogene Beweismittel in Strafverfahren dar. Eine möglichst unbeeinflusste Beurteilung ihrer Glaubwürdigkeit ist insbesondere dann von zentraler Bedeutung, wenn keine weiteren Beweise vorliegen. Empirische Befunde deuten jedoch darauf hin, dass die Bewertung der Glaubwürdigkeit von Zeug:innen nicht ausschließlich auf rechtlich relevanten Kriterien basiert, sondern auch durch sogenannte extralegale Faktoren beeinflusst werden kann, die außerhalb des rechtlich zulässigen Entscheidungsrahmens liegen. Polizeibeamt:innen treten regelmäßig als Zeug:innen vor Gericht auf, etwa als Tatzeug:innen, sachverständige Zeug:innen oder Zeug:innen eigener Ermittlungen. Aufgrund ihrer beruflichen Ausbildung und zugeschriebenen Expertise werden sie im Allgemeinen als besonders glaubwürdig wahrgenommen. Darüber hinaus ist das Tragen einer Polizeiuniform mit positiven stereotypen Zuschreibungen assoziiert. Bislang ist jedoch kaum empirisch untersucht, inwieweit beruflicher Status und Uniformierung die Glaubwürdigkeitsbeurteilung in gerichtlichen Entscheidungssituationen tatsächlich beeinflussen. Die vorliegende experimentelle Online-Studie (N = 290) untersuchte daher den Einfluss des beruflichen Status sowie der Kleidung auf die wahrgenommene Glaubwürdigkeit eines männlichen Zeugen (Zivilperson in Zivilkleidung vs. Polizeibeamter in Zivilkleidung vs. Polizeibeamter in Uniform). Den Teilnehmenden wurden ein Foto des Zeugen sowie eine Audioaufnahme einer fiktiven Zeugenaussage präsentiert. Die Glaubwürdigkeit wurde mithilfe der Witness Credibility Scale (Brodsky et al., 2010) erfasst. Es zeigte sich kein Unterschied zwischen den drei Gruppen im Hinblick auf die Gesamtglaubwürdigkeit. Auf den Subskalen Fachkompetenz und Vertrauenswürdigkeit wurden die polizeilichen Zeugen jedoch positiver bewertet als der zivile Zeuge. Die Befunde legen nahe, dass weniger die äußere Erscheinung, sondern insbesondere der berufliche Status einzelne Dimensionen der Zeug:innenbeurteilung beeinflussen und somit potenziell zu gerichtlichen Entscheidungsprozessen beitragen kann.

403. Wenn „später“ zu „nie“ wird: Eine domänenspezifische Analyse von Prokrastination und Selbstmitgefühl in den Bereichen Sport, Schlaf und Zahnarztbesuche.
Olga Rapoport | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Olga Rapoport | Germany
Eva Neidhardt | University of Koblenz | Germany

Das Unterlassen von gesundheitsförderndem Verhalten ist ein weitverbreitetes Phänomen mit gravierenden Folgen. Während Prokrastination traditionell als akademisches Problem betrachtet wurde, rückt ihre Rolle als Selbstregulationsdefizit im Gesundheitskontext zunehmend in den Fokus. Ziel der vorliegenden Arbeit war es, den Einfluss domänenspezifischer Prokrastination auf das Gesundheitsverhalten sowie die potenzielle Pufferwirkung von Selbstmitgefühl in drei unterschiedlichen Domänen (Sport, Schlaf und Zahnarztbesuche) zu untersuchen. Die Datengrundlage bilden drei Studien: zwei Tagebuchstudien zu den Themen Sport (über einen Zeitraum von sieben Wochen) und Schlaf (über einen Zeitraum von einer Woche) sowie eine Querschnittstudie zu Zahnarztbesuchen mit einem neu entwickelten Erhebungsinstrument. Die Ergebnisse zeigen konsistent, dass domänenspezifische Prokrastination in allen untersuchten Bereichen einen signifikanten negativen Einfluss auf das direkte Verhalten hat und in den Längsschnittstudien einen vergrößernden Effekt auf die Intentions-Handlungs-Lücke zeigt. Dieser Effekt war stärker als der der allgemeinen Prokrastination. Entgegen der Annahme eines generell positiven Effekts von Selbstmitgefühl auf die Gesundheit zeigte sich dieser nur differenziert. Während Selbstmitgefühl sich positiv auf die Schlafqualität und -zufriedenheit auswirkte, zeigte es keinen Haupteffekt auf das Sportverhalten oder die Zahnarztbesuche. Im Sportbereich fungierte Selbstmitgefühl jedoch als Moderator und eliminierte den negativen Einfluss der Prokrastination auf die Intentions-Handlungs-Lücke bei hoch selbstfürsorglichen Personen. Die Befunde verdeutlichen die Notwendigkeit einer domänenspezifischen Betrachtung von Prokrastination und zeigen, dass Selbstmitgefühl keine universelle Ressource ist, sondern kontextabhängig als Strategie zur Emotionsregulation wirksam wird.

404. Einflüsse von temporalen Veränderungen der Achtsamkeit auf Organizational Citizenship Behavior: Die moderierende Rolle des Leistungsmotivs.
Alexander Winkler | Bergische Universität Wuppertal - Fakultät für Wirtschaftswissenschaft | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Alexander Winkler | Bergische Universität Wuppertal - Fakultät für Wirtschaftswissenschaft | Germany
Dr. Elvira Radaca | Bergische Universität Wuppertal - Fakultät für Wirtschaftswissenschaft | Germany
Prof. Dr. Stefan Diestel | Bergische Universität Wuppertal - Fakultät für Wirtschaftswissenschaft | Germany

In den letzten Jahren fanden Achtsamkeitsveränderungen im Tagesverlauf und ihre Auswirkungen auf das Arbeitsverhalten zunehmend Beachtung in der Literatur. Unklar bleibt jedoch, wie sich Achtsamkeitsveränderungen im Tagesverlauf auf Organizational Citizenship Behavior (OCB) am selben Tag auswirken. Die Theorie der Persönlichkeits-System-Interaktionen (PSI-Theorie) lässt vermuten, dass verstärkte Achtsamkeit über zunehmende positive Affektzustände tagesspezifisches OCB vorhersagt. Demnach werden durch Achtsamkeit zielgerichtete Regulations- und Motivationsprozesse begünstigt, die Beschäftigte veranlassen, zusätzliche Leistungsbeiträge einzubringen. Darüber hinaus lässt sich aus der PSI-Theorie ableiten, dass das Leistungsmotiv eine zentrale Rolle bei der Bildung von Absichten einnimmt und den tagesspezifischen Zusammenhang zwischen Affektveränderungen und OCB moderiert. Das Leistungsmotiv beschreibt als Disposition das Ausmaß, in dem es einer Person wichtig ist, herausfordernde Ziele durch Verhaltensanstrengung zu erreichen. In der Literatur finden sich Hinweise darauf, dass Yoga-Praktizierende im Verlauf eines Tages eine stärkere Steigerung positiver Affekte erfahren als Nicht-Yoga-Praktizierende. Wir nehmen an, dass diese Steigerung mit einer Achtsamkeitssteigerung zusammenhängt. Aus diesem Grund sind Yoga-Praktizierende die Zielgruppe dieser Untersuchung, da wir erwarten, die zu untersuchenden Phänomene eher in dieser Gruppe zu beobachten. Auf der Grundlage einer sich aus 62 berufstätigen Personen zusammensetzenden Stichprobe haben wir in einer Tagebuchstudie (10 Arbeitstage und vier Messzeitpunkte pro Tage) zeigen können, dass Änderungen des positiven Affekts den positiven Zusammenhang zwischen tagesspezifischen Achtsamkeitsveränderungen und OCB mediieren. Ferner moderiert (verstärkt) das Leistungsmotiv den Zusammenhang zwischen Änderungen des positiven Affekts und OCB. Die Ergebnisse erlauben differenzierte Einblicke in die Wirkung von Achtsamkeit auf Affektänderungen und OCB unter Einfluss des Leistungsmotivs.

405. Pre-Ratings in Evaluative Learning
Claudine Pulm | University of Cologne | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Claudine Pulm | University of Cologne | Germany
Lea Sperlich | University of Cologne | Germany
Anne Gast | University of Cologne | Germany
Olivier Corneille | University of Cologne; Université catholique de Louvain | Belgium

Evaluative conditioning (EC) research deals with the question of how we form attitudes toward conditioned stimuli (CSs) by pairing them with positive or negative unconditioned stimuli (USs). In the present studies (N = 296; N = 527), we experimentally investigated whether measuring the attitude toward the CSs (and in Study 2, the USs) before conditioning influences the EC effect. We reasoned that assessing participants’ attitudes before conditioning might signal the importance of this judgment and thereby alter subsequent evaluations (e.g., through conversational norms/experimental demands). Participants either rated their liking of the CSs (and in Study 2, of the USs) both before and after conditioning or only after conditioning. Results showed an EC effect and, more importantly, that the magnitude of the EC effect did not differ between groups when only the liking of the CSs was assessed. When the liking of the CSs and USs was assessed, the EC effect was smaller in the pre-rating condition. These findings have implications for research on attitude formation, as they suggest that pre-ratings of CSs do not systematically bias conditioned attitudes, while additionally assessing US attitudes might influence the EC effect (e.g., through calibration effects).

406. Angst vor Elterngesprächen bei Lehramtsstudierenden: Zusammenhänge mit Kontroll- und Wertüberzeugungen
Sabrina M. Kleine | Universität Bielefeld | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Sabrina M. Kleine | Universität Bielefeld | Germany
Prof. Dr. Elke Wild | Universität Bielefeld | Germany

Elterngespräche sind ein zentraler Bestandteil der Kooperation von Elternhaus und Schule und stellen für (angehende) Lehrkräfte eine komplexe Aufgabe dar (Sacher, 2022; Sauer, 2017). Studien zeigen, dass (angehende) Lehrkräfte den Kontakt mit Eltern als bedeutsam ansehen, jedoch häufig Angst davor empfinden und die Vorbereitung auf diese Gespräche als unzureichend bewerten (D’Haem & Griswold, 2017; Nuding et al., 2018). Emotionen im Zusammenhang mit Elterngesprächen wurden bislang selten und überwiegend qualitativ untersucht. Auf Grundlage der Kontroll-Wert-Theorie (Pekrun, 2006, 2018, 2024), nach der die wahrgenommene Kontrolle und der wahrgenommene Wert einer Aufgabe zentral für die Entstehung von Emotionen sind, wird in diesem Beitrag untersucht, inwiefern Selbstwirksamkeitserwartungen (wahrgenommene Kontrolle) in Bezug auf die Beratung, den Umgang mit Konflikten und die Beziehungsgestaltung sowie der intrinsische und extrinsische Wert dieser Gespräche mit der Angst vor dem Führen von Elterngesprächen bei Lehramtsstudierenden zusammenhängen. Unseres Wissens wurden die Annahmen der Kontroll-Wert-Theorie bislang noch nicht auf diesen Kontext übertragen. Die Untersuchung basiert auf querschnittlichen Online-Fragebogendaten des Wintersemesters 2024/25 von N = 407 Lehramtsstudierenden (Bachelor, Master, erstes Staatsexamen) von 17 deutschen Universitäten bzw. Hochschulen. Die Zusammenhänge wurden mithilfe eines Strukturgleichungsmodells unter Einbezug relevanter Kontrollvariablen analysiert. Die Selbstwirksamkeitserwartung in Bezug auf die Beziehungsgestaltung sowie der extrinsische Wert zeigten signifikante positive Zusammenhänge mit der Angst vor Elterngesprächen, während die Selbstwirksamkeitserwartung in Bezug auf den Umgang mit Konflikten sowie der intrinsische Wert signifikant negativ mit der Angst vor diesen assoziiert waren. Die Befunde verdeutlichen die Notwendigkeit, dem Thema in der ersten Phase der Lehrkräftebildung mehr Bedeutung beizumessen.

407. Using computational modelling and fMRI to study peer influences on empathy formation
Dr. Anne Saulin | University of Birmingham, UK | United Kingdom
Show details
Authors:
Dr. Anne Saulin | University of Birmingham, UK | United Kingdom
Prof. Patricia Lockwood | University of Birmingham, UK
Dr. Lei Zhang | University of Birmingham, UK

Empathy and prosocial behavior toward strangers are vital for societal cohesion and cooperation. While much is known about individual empathy responses, less is understood about how social context—particularly peer group norms—influences empathy formation and prosocial decisions. In this pre-registered study (https://tinyurl.com/47v7pjj2), we investigate how observing others in pain is modulated by the empathy norms of surrounding peers. Participants viewed a target individual receiving painful stimulation while embedded within either a highly empathic or low-empathy peer group context. We applied a computational social learning model to quantify how peer group empathy norms shape the formation of empathic responses and influence subsequent prosocial behavior in a binary dictator game.
Preliminary findings suggest that participants show stronger empathy formation in the presence of highly empathic peers, whereas low-empathy peer contexts do not significantly diminish empathic responses. Notably, this social modulation of empathy does not appear to consistently translate into changes in trial-by-trial prosocial decision-making.
In the next phase of the study, we will integrate computational modeling with functional magnetic resonance imaging to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying peer-modulated empathy. Based on prior research, we expect key contributions from the anterior insula, anterior cingulate cortex, and temporo-parietal junction—regions consistently implicated in affective resonance, conflict monitoring, and social perspective-taking.
These findings offer insight into how social environments shape empathic processing and its translation into behavior, with implications for understanding the development and plasticity of prosociality in group contexts.

408. Modeling Trust Dynamics in Repeated Interactions: An Agent-Based Approach
Karoline Misch | Technische Universität Braunschweig | Germany
Show details

Nils Müller | Technische Universität Braunschweig | Germany
Jan de Haan | Technische Universität Braunschweig | Germany
Dr. Farina Wille | Technische Universität Braunschweig | Germany

Trust is a highly relevant topic, particularly in times of social and technological uncertainty. Beyond defining what trust is, an important question concerns its temporal dynamics: How does trust change over repeated interactions and which factors influence whether interactions remain stable or gradually deteriorate?
The present work proposes an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach as a suitable method for studying trust dynamics in repeated interactions. In the model, agents make sequential cooperation decisions under uncertainty based on perceived trust signals and prior interaction outcomes. Outcomes feed back into an internal trust value, which in turn influences subsequent decisions. Trust is thus represented as a dynamic variable that evolves over time depending on interaction history and other contextual factors.
Rather than aiming to provide a comprehensive theory of trust, the model serves as a formal framework to systematically explore how different decision rules, thresholds and payoff structures shape the development and stability of interactions. By varying key parameters, it becomes possible to identify patterns in how trust increases, stabilizes, fluctuates, or declines across repeated exchanges.
The approach makes visible how specific outcomes influence trust trajectories over time and how these trajectories feed back into future cooperation decisions. While the initial focus lies on dyadic interactions, the framework can, as an extension, be applied to multi-agent settings, allowing the exploration of broader interaction patterns that emerge from repeated local exchanges.

409. Investigating the Influence of Infant-Directed Speech on Attention and Visual Processing: An ERP and Gamma Activity Study
Milena Marx | Heidelberg University | Germany

Prof. Dr. Stefanie Peykarjou | Charlotte Fresenius University Wiesbaden

Evidence suggests that infant attention for and learning of speech stimuli is enhanced by infant-directed speech (IDS), characterized by a higher mean pitch and higher variability in prosody. Much less is known regarding the potential general effect of IDS on cognitive processes, such as attention and learning during the encoding and processing of visual or multimodal information. 35 four-month-olds were tested in an EEG cueing paradigm comparing IDS and adult-directed speech (ADS) as cues for visual input. During the cueing phase, infants saw an object while hearing a short prompt ("Look here") spoken either in IDS or ADS. The same object was then shown again, allowing to assess how the preceding speech register shaped attention to the visual stimulus.
Our primary outcome variables were the Nc and PSW ERPs during the subsequent object presentation. While the Nc is a well-established index of infants' attentional engagement with visual stimuli, the PSW has been linked to memory updating. Preliminary analyses indicate larger Nc amplitudes for objects previously cued by IDS compared to ADS, while no difference in PSW was observed. Results suggest that IDS may boost attentional engagement with visual input, pointing to a broader cognitive influence of IDS beyond speech processing.
Secondary analyses will examine oscillatory dynamics during cueing. We predict increased gamma synchronization over frontal regions, indicative of attentional focus, while listening to IDS. Overall, this study provides evidence that the speech register of everyday caregiver prompts can shape infants' attention to visual information, with implications for early multimodal learning.

Melina Posch | Leipzig University | Germany

Proactive behavior at work entails employees’ self-initiated actions aimed at changing the work environment or themselves. Research suggests that employees’ proactive work behavior is linked to their affective states, both as a predictor and as an outcome. However, there is limited knowledge and partially inconclusive results on how proactive behavior is related to affect of different valence (i.e., positive or negative) and activation (i.e., high or low activated). In studying such affective predictors and consequences of proactivity, it is important to consider individuals’ dispositional tendency to engage in proactive behavior, namely their proactive personality. The aim of this preregistered daily diary study is to investigate relations between personal initiative and affect, conditional upon proactive personality. We examine how affect before work (positive and negative, high and low activated) is related to personal initiative at work, how personal initiative at work is related to affect after work, and whether proactive personality facilitates these relations. Data were collected via two daily surveys across ten workdays. The results of the data analysis will be available by the time of the conference. This study contributes to our understanding of the complex affective processes related to proactive behavior at work and the role of proactive personality.

411. Career aspirations in elementary and middle school: The influence of gender stereotypes and counter-stereotypical role models
Johanna Landvogt | University of Bamberg | Germany

Prof. Dr. Jan Lenhart | University of Bamberg | Germany

According to relevant theories and research, career aspirations begin to emerge already during childhood. The present study examined the influence of occupational gender stereotypes and exposure to counter-stereotypical role models on school children’s career aspirations. Thirteen occupations (5 typically female, 5 typically male, 3 neutral), which had been rated by adults concerning gender stereotypicity in a pilot study, were presented to elementary and middle school children (N = 299, ages 7 to 16). Children’s stereotypes and interest in these occupations, as well as their assessment of the gender-stereotypicity of their parents' occupations, and their own interest in their parents’ occupations were assessed. Furthermore, the number, frequency, and familiarity with counter-stereotypical role models were collected. Preliminary results showed, as hypothesized, that children assumed that girls are significantly more interested in “typically feminine” occupations (t(297) = 23.01, p < .001, d = 1.33) and boys in “typically masculine” occupations (t(297) = 26.44, p < .001, d = 1.53). Children’s own career aspiration also showed gender differences, with girls being more interested in “typically feminine” occupations (t(293) = -9.92, p < .001, d = -1.16) and boys in “typically masculine” occupations (t(293) = 7.44, p < .001, d = 0.87). There was no significant decrease (i.e. flexibility) of gender-stereotypicity (mean of differences between interest ratings for girls and boys for each occupation) with age (r = -.02, p = .753). Analyses on the influence of counter-stereotypical role models are still pending.

412. Zwischen Autonomie und Verantwortung: Eine qualitative Interviewstudie zu Geschwisterrollen in Familien mit einem Kind mit geistiger Behinderung
Dr. Regina Weißmann | Katholische Universität Eichstätt-Ingolstadt | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Dr. Regina Weißmann | Katholische Universität Eichstätt-Ingolstadt | Germany
Coralie Englberger | Katholische Universität Eichstätt-Ingolstadt
Stella Ströbele | Katholische Universität Eichstätt-Ingolstadt

Familien mit einem Kind mit geistiger Behinderung sind mit spezifischen Anforderungen konfrontiert. Eltern müssen unterschiedliche Autonomie- und Schutzbedarfe ihrer Kinder mit und ohne Behinderung ausbalancieren. Geschwister ohne Behinderung bewegen sich dabei in einem Spannungsfeld zwischen Verantwortungsübernahme, Anpassung und eigener Lebensgestaltung. Die vorliegende qualitative Interviewstudie verfolgt das Ziel, ein tiefgehendes Verständnis für die Rolle von Geschwistern in Familien mit einem Kind mit geistiger Behinderung zu erlangen. Das Material umfasst N=32 Interviews – darunter 5 Interviews mit Elternpaaren, 10 Interviews einzelner Elternteile und 17 Interviews mit Geschwistern – teilweise in dyadischer Eltern-Kind-Konstellation. In der inhaltsanalytischen Auswertung (Kuckartz & Rädiker, 2022) wurden drei übergeordnete Cluster identifiziert: 1) Geschwister in kompensatorisch-verantwortungsüberladener Rolle, die durch starke Parentifizierung, hohes Pflichtgefühl, deutliche Autonomieeinbußen und Zukunftssorgen geprägt ist, 2) Geschwister in ambivalenten Beziehungskonstellationen, die sich durch wechselnde Nähe-Distanz und einen Konflikt zwischen Loyalität und Abgrenzung beschreiben lassen, 3) Geschwister in resiliente und ressourcenorientierten Konstellationen, deren familiäres Konstrukt sich durch emotionale Nähe, gemäßigte Verantwortungsübernahme sowie elterliche Anerkennung auszeichnet. Die Elternperspektive verdeutlicht eine gleichzeitige Wahrnehmung der Geschwisterrolle als hoch belastet und potenziell entwicklungsförderlich. Eltern schildern intensive Bemühungen, Aufmerksamkeit und Zuwendung zu balancieren und Entlastung zu gewährleisten. Die Auswertung der Dyaden zeigt dabei neben deckungsgleiche Schilderungen auch abweichende Perspektiven: Während ihre Eltern Entlastungsstrategien hervorheben, berichten einige Geschwister weiterhin von Überverantwortung und unzureichender Berücksichtigung eigener Bedürfnisse. Die Ergebnisse verdeutlichen, dass Geschwisterkinder ohne Behinderung spezifische Unterstützungsbedarfe aufweisen. Dies weist auf die Relevanz von familienzentrierten und bio-psycho-sozialen Unterstützungsansätzen hin. Praxisimplikationen ergeben sich insbesondere für Beratungsangebote, die auf Geschwisterautonomie und intrafamiliäre Ausbalancierung von Verantwortlichkeit abzielen.

413. Valence asymmetries in Evaluative Conditioning: The undue influence of group members
Lea Sperlich | Universität zu Köln | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Lea Sperlich | Universität zu Köln | Germany
Prof. Dr. Christian Unkelbach | Universtät zu Köln

Evaluative Conditioning (EC) describes how our preferences change when neutral stimuli (conditioned stimuli, CSs) are repeatedly paired with positive or negative information (unconditioned stimuli, USs). Interestingly, unlike in many other cognitive domains, typical EC experiments do not show a negativity bias: CSs paired with negative USs are not evaluated more extremely than CSs paired with positive USs (Sperlich & Unkelbach, 2025).

A cognitive-ecological account explains this symmetry: positive and negative information typically occur with equal frequency in EC paradigms. Under such balanced conditions, no bias occurs. However, when one type of information is rare, asymmetries arise: rare negative information produces a negativity bias, while rare positive information produces a positivity bias.

This raises an important question: Do such asymmetries also shape how we evaluate groups? In other words, can rare group members disproportionately influence how we perceive an entire group — a pattern potentially relevant to stereotype formation?

To address this, we conducted four pre-registered online experiments (N = 2,404). To test whether rare group members alter evaluations of the group as a whole, we paired rare and frequent group members (CSs) with positive and negative animal pictures (USs).

Across all experiments, the findings show that individual group members can exert a disproportionate influence on evaluations of the entire group.

Peter Haehner | Charlotte Fresenius University, Düsseldorf, Germany
Janina Larissa Bühler | University of Freiburg, Germany

Theoretical reasoning suggests that personality can change in response to life events, but meta-analytic evidence documents weak or absent effects of such changes. This discrepancy may be due to the ways in which life events are conceptualized and measured. Specifically, little is known about the role of event characteristics (i.e., event features such as the timing) and proximal mechanisms (i.e., immediate shifts in daily life such as new routines). To address this, we develop and validate an empirically grounded taxonomy of the characteristics and mechanisms associated with life events. First, to develop the taxonomy, we use open-ended narratives from 903 participants and apply an inductive-deductive coding procedure to the data. Second, to validate the taxonomy, we examine its predictive power for immediate and long-term changes in personality states and traits. Together, this taxonomy aids both the sorting and understanding of the specific features associated with life events, offering a more detailed examination of daily and long-term personality changes.

Previous research (Kaufmann et al., 2025) has shown that early childcare in Luxembourg promotes early language skills in Luxembourgish in those who struggle the most with this language - a promising finding for Luxembourg, where educational gaps based on home language and socioeconomic status are especially large (Hornung et al., 2021; SCRIPT, 2020). The present study aims to exploratively investigate whether such moderating effects might extend to the domains of reading and mathematics and to timepoints beyond first grade, as Luxembourg's highly funded, yet heterogenous and partly privatized childcare system combines characteristics that might facilitate either fadeout or persistence of childcare associations with academic achievement over time (Esping-Andersen et al., 2012). Using large-scale school monitoring data from multilingual Luxembourg from 2018 to 2023 of a cohort of around 4,000 students, hierarchical linear regression on fifth grade mathematics and reading comprehension, as well as grade retention will be conducted, investigating the association to early childcare ("crèche", for under four year olds) and its moderation by socioeconomic status and home language. Family and child background factors and previous performance are included as control variables. Results on moderating effects will help shed light on whether childcare in the diverse and multilingual setting of Luxembourg might alleviate educational inequalities by boosting especially the academic achievement of disadvantaged student groups.

The role of age, especially adolescence, in conspiracy beliefs has recently received increased attention (Bordeleau & Stockemer, 2025; Hornsey et al., 2025; Imhoff & Bertlich, 2026). Although the available evidence is still too preliminary to conclude that conspiracy beliefs peak during adolescence, the school context warrants attention in conspiracy-belief research given schools’ central role in political socialization (Noack & Eckstein, 2023). So far, the role of the school context, and teachers in particular, remains largely unexplored. The available research suggests that teachers often feel they lack time, didactic tools, competence, and knowledge to respond adequately to conspiracy theories in the classroom (Bergane, 2024; Dyrendal & Jolley, 2020; Jerome et al., 2024). These studies indicate that many teachers feel insufficiently prepared, but they do not directly assess teachers’ self-efficacy for responding to conspiracy theories. We therefore investigated whether exposure to a conspiratorial (vs. non-conspiratorial) student statement reduces pre-service teachers’ self-efficacy and whether emotional responses help explain this effect, taking into account classic self-efficacy sources (Bandura, 1997). To this end, we conducted a preregistered experiment with 397 pre-service teachers at German universities who read a vignette with either a conspiratorial or non-conspiratorial remark by a student. Results of a parallel multiple mediation model indicated that the teacher students in the conspiracy condition reported lower self-efficacy than participants in the no-conspiracy condition. This effect was mediated in parallel by anger, anxiety, and calmness. Exploratorily, we also examined pre-service teachers’ behavioral intentions for how they would respond in this situation. Practical implications are discussed.

417. Equal Potential, Unequal Capital? Perceived Founders’ Success Potential and Capital Allocation in Startup Funding across Investor Types
Louisa Güthing-Rinsdorf | TH Köln (Cologne University of Applied Sciences) | Germany

Laura Traußnig | University of Graz
Prof. Dr. Sabine Bergner | University of Graz | Austria
Prof. Dr. Dr. Carolin Palmer | Technical University of Applied Sciences Augsburg

The gender funding gap remains a persistent phenomenon in real-world startup financing, yet empirical findings are mixed. One explanation may lie in sample differences, raising questions about external validity, contextual influences and psychological mechanisms. To address this, we compare how novices and professional investors assess male and female founders in terms of perceived success potential and how strongly these perceptions translate into capital allocation. In a within-subject vignette experiment, students (N = 221), business angels (N = 35), and institutional investors (N = 39) evaluated startup pitches randomly assigned to male or female founders.
Mixed-effects analyses reveal significant group differences in perceived success potential: students attribute higher perceived success potentials to male founders, business angels evaluate male and female founders as equally promising, and institutional investors attribute higher perceived success potentials to female founders. Although perceived success potential strongly predicts capital allocation across all groups, not only students but also business angels allocate more capital to male founders. Moreover, institutional investors’ perceptual advantage for female founders does not translate into significantly higher capital allocations.
Overall, our findings highlight subjective perceptions of founders’ success potential – potentially shaped by gender stereotypes and decision contexts – as psychological mechanisms underlying capital allocation. At the same time, gender funding gaps do not necessarily stem from lower perceived success potentials attributed to female founders. Instead, disparities may emerge through additional mechanisms operating beyond or independently of perceived founders’ success potential. Implications for research, investor training, and institutional bias-reduction strategies are discussed.

To understand the advantages of high-quality leader-member exchange (LMX) for followers and leaders beyond social exchange theory (cf. The statistical analyses of the collected data will be completed before September 2026. Study 1 will test the hypothesized mediation model for followers. Study 2 will test the hypothesized mediation model for both followers and leaders while also providing an assessment of LMX by both parties and an assessment of the follower’s personal initiative by the leader.
With these two studies, we contribute to prior literature in several ways. First, we contribute to LMX research by proposing work-related sense of coherence as a psychological and health-focused mediator that connects LMX with sickness absence, stress, and personal initiative. Second, we contribute to research on work-related sense of coherence by implementing LMX as a further predictor. 419. Riemannian Clustering as a Preprocessing Tool for Meta-Analytic Structural Equation Modeling"
Christian Bloszies | Friedrich-Schiller Universität Jena | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Prof. Dr. Tobias Koch | Friedrich-Schiller Universität Jena | Germany
Christian Bloszies | Friedrich-Schiller Universität Jena | Germany

When using meta-analytic structural equation modeling (MASEM), one major challenge is how to handle study heterogeneity. Random-effects methods are a common way to account for study-level heterogeneity by assuming variability of population correlation matrices across studies. Heterogeneity can also be explained by including study-level moderators. While both approaches can be effective, they cannot explicitly account for heterogeneity that is caused by structurally different population models (e.g. different factor structures) since the final estimation step is an SEM with a specific given structure. In the ideal case, relevant subgroups are known (e.g. through theory, known explanatory variables) and subgroup analyses are possible. If subgroups are not known, or researchers want to explore their data to find patterns of more homogenous subgroups, clustering approaches can be useful tools as a preprocessing step before conducting MASEM analyses.

In previous simulation studies, correlation matrices were clustered as vectors in Euclidean space. This approach showed satisfactory results but ignored the inherent geometric structure of correlation matrices, which are embedded in a Riemannian (i.e. non-Euclidean) space, where different definitions of length and distance apply. Riemannian clustering respects this geometry of correlation matrices as mathematical objects and offers a potential improvement over vector-based clustering by preserving the structure of study correlation matrices.

We present a simulation study comparing Euclidean and Riemannian clustering performance when heterogeneity was induced by structurally different population models. We discuss the advantages and disadvantages of non-Euclidean clustering for recovering homogeneous subgroups and the implications for preprocessing MASEM data.

420. Hot Topics in Science Communication Research and Psychology’s Contribution
Amelie Kröger | Leibniz Institute for Psychology (ZPID), Trier, Germany | Germany

Dr. André Bittermann | Leibniz Institute for Psychology (ZPID), Trier, Germany | Germany
Jun.-Prof. Dr. Marlene Altenmüller | Leibniz Institute for Psychology (ZPID), Trier, Germany

The scientific interest in science communication as a research topic is currently experiencing a sharp increase - also in psychology. Anecdotally, the field of science communication research has been formed by many societal developments and challenges such as the dawn of large-scale social media use and, more recently, the Covid-19 pandemic. However, do we see this also reflected systematically in the topics studied in science communication research? And what do psychological researchers focus on the most? To determine these “hot topics” that shape the field, we inspected three leading journals for science communication research: The Journal of Science Communication, Science Communication, and Public Understanding of Science. We retrieved 4,138 publication records from OpenAlex and conducted bibliometric analyses on titles, abstracts and keywords with the bibliometrix R package. Leveraging community detection, density, and centrality in word co-occurrence networks, we found themes that were classified as being either emerging, declining, basic, niche, or motor themes. The latter are understood as the current research focus and comprise topics such as climate change, media outlets and citizen science. Additionally, we inspected topical change from 1992 until 2026. This demonstrates that topics such as public engagement and the covid pandemic gained notable attention in science communication research in recent years. Overall, our bibliometric analysis highlights that psychology as a discipline is an increasingly active player in science communication research and can contribute theoretically and empirically to many of its current hot topics.

421. Custom Contrast Matrices for Interindividual Differences in Experimental Effects (semnova in R)
Marcel Koppka | Bielefeld University | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Marcel Koppka | Bielefeld University | Germany
Prof. Dr. Axel Mayer | Bielefeld University | Germany
Dr. Benedikt Langenberg | Maastricht University | Netherlands

Interindividual differences can be large in how people respond to the same experimental manipulation. When focusing on average effects, these differences may not be apparent. For example, an experimental manipulation may improve outcomes on average, while some people improve a lot, others improve only slightly and a few show no improvement or even worsen.
To examine these differences with specific hypotheses, custom contrast matrices provide a flexible way to define planned comparisons, including main effects, interactions and more complex contrasts (e.g., higher order interactions). This submission presents a practical workflow for using custom contrasts to model experimental effects and interindividual differences in structural equation modeling. The workflow is implemented in the R package semnova. It applies to within-subject designs and designs that include both within and between subject factors, with manifest or latent outcomes.
An applied example from longitudinal reading research demonstrates how custom contrast matrices specify interpretable effect components and how these effects are estimated. The example contrasts regular versus Landolt sentences across Grades 1, 2 and 4 and uses eye-tracking indicators (e.g., re-fixation time, fixation count, initial landing position) to assess reading efficiency. In semnova, interindividual differences are represented as variability in contrast-defined effects, so that both average effects and variability across individuals can be estimated and reported.
The goal is to provide an accessible introduction to custom contrasts in semnova and to facilitate reproducible use in experimental research.

Prof. Dr. Jörg-Henrik Heine | Universität der Bundeswehr München

Ausgehend vom Modell subjektiver Klassenkonflikte nach Schmidt (1982) wird untersucht, inwiefern sich Konfliktmilieus als typische Muster individueller Konfliktwahrnehmung in Deutschland identifizieren lassen und welche Bedeutung diese für das Vertrauen in Politiker und politische Institutionen haben (z.B. Anhut & Heitmeyer, 2014). Theoretisch knüpft der Ansatz an das Stufenmodell des Klassenbewusstseins von Giddens (1975) an und versteht Einschätzungen zu gesellschaftlichen Interessengegensätzen als Indikatoren wahrgenommener Klassenkonflikte.
Der vorliegende Beitrag ist eine vergleichende Analyse auf Basis der ALLBUS - Daten 2010 und 2021 (GESIS - Leibniz-Institut für Sozialwissenschaften, 2024). Aufgrund von Stichprobenausfall und Oversampling in Ostdeutschland verwenden alle Analysen gewichtete Daten. Zur Strukturierung der Konfliktwahrnehmung werden elf Konflikt-Items (u. a. Arbeitgeber vs. Arbeitnehmer, Politiker vs. einfache Bürger, Arm vs. Reich) zunächst mit einer Hauptkomponentenanalyse (HPK) geprüft. Anschließend werden mittels einer hierarchischen Clusteranalyse nach dem Ward-Verfahren auf Basis der Ladungsmatrix aus der HPK die Items zu Konfliktmilieus zusammengefasst.
Für beide Erhebungszeitpunkte (2010 und 2021) lassen sich drei Konfliktmilieus (Generation, Politik, Status) identifizieren. Für personenzentrierte Analysen (vgl. Heine, Alexandrowicz & Stemmler, 2025; Heine & Stemmler, 2021) werden dichotome Klassifikationen der drei Konfliktmilieus (hohes vs. niedriges Konfliktpotential) sowie des Vertrauens in politische Institutionen gebildet. Die Auswertung erfolgt mittels Konfigurationsfrequenzanalyse (KFA) als Residualanalyse im Rahmen loglinearer Modelle. Im Haupteffektmodell zeigen sich insbesondere im politischen Konfliktmilieu Konfigurationen hohen Konfliktpotentials in Verbindung mit fehlendem Vertrauen. Im Prädiktionsmodell ergeben sich keine bedeutsamen Modellabweichungen, was auf eine robuste Vorhersage des institutionellen Vertrauens durch Konfliktmilieu-Konfigurationen hinweist. Die Ergebnisse sprechen für eine zeitliche Stabilität zentraler Konfliktstrukturen zwischen 2010 und 2021.

423. Situational stimulation of accommodative responses - Experimental investigation of developmental regulatory processes
Chantal Janßen | University of Hildesheim | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Chantal Janßen | University of Hildesheim | Germany
Annemarie Koch | University of Hildesheim
Prof. Dr. Dirk Wentura | Universität des Saarlandes | Germany
Prof. Dr. Werner Greve | University of Hildesheim

The investigation of developmental regulatory processes has largely focused on examining individual differences in the availability or usage of these processes. Prototypical for this is research on flexible goal adjustment (FGA), an important mechanism of adaptive self-regulation (Brandtstädter & Rothermund, 2002). The importance of FGA and various sub-processes (goal disengagement and goal reengagement; Kappes & Schattke, 2022; Loidl & Leipold, 2019: Wrosch et al., 2003) for well-being and quality of life (e.g., Barlow et al., 2022; Hanssen et al., 2015) has been investigated almost exclusively in cross-sectional correlational moderator analyses (self-assessment), without directly measuring the processes and their effects (for similar approaches, see Heckhausen et al., 2010). Experimental approaches in which goal adjustments were measured in response to induced goal blockages (Rühs et al., 2022, 2025) indicate that goal adjustments are a possible response, but have not yet demonstrated protective effects. Experimental approaches that attempted to specifically induce accommodative processes of FGA have yielded mixed results (Leipold et al., 2014). The presentation will discuss possible explanations for this and present an experimental (priming) paradigm that is supposed to specifically stimulate accommodative reactions. Data from a first pilot study (N=110) suggest that reactions to vignettes with goal blockages (e.g., losing a legal case, major travel obstacles) can be influenced by the previously induced “accommodative processing mode” (Brandtstädter & Rothermund, 2002). This example also underscores the underestimated importance of experimental studies for investigating developmental regulatory processes.

424. Physical activity and stress: a diary study
Lotta Loerbroks | Leuphana Lüneburg | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Lotta Loerbroks | Leuphana Lüneburg | Germany
Prof. Dr. Philipp Alexander Freund | Leuphana Lüneburg

Physical activity has been shown to improve bodily and mental well-being, especially when upheld persistently. However, perceived stress can lead to diminished physical activity or disruption of an exercise regime. While this bi-directional relationship has been examined within university students in a short-term diary study, the mid- to long-term effects have not been sufficiently explored in lay people.
Moreover, facets of Self-Determination Theory (i.e., forms of motivation, goal-orientation, perceived fulfilment of basic psychological needs) have been shown to correlate with higher levels of physical activity. Whether these facets hold predictive value for persistent physical activity and if they might counteract perceived stress levels has yet to be determined.
To better understand the bi-directional relationship between physical activity and stress and the potential influences of Self-Determination Theory’s facets over time, we conducted an Experience Sampling Method study. Participants reported their motivation, goal orientation and perceived fulfilment of basic psychological needs at the beginning and end of an 8-week period. During the 8 weeks participants received a bi-weekly prompt and reported physical activity and perceived stress since the last prompt. This allows us to better understand the intricate relationship between physical activity and stress in lay people over time. Data collection has been completed, and data assessment will be finished by September 2026.
Understanding how physical activity and experienced stress affect each other may serve as a vital contribution to evidence-based interventions that can help to increase and stabilize lay people’s long-term physical activity and therefore their overall physical and mental well-being.

425. Validierung der Fremdversion der Creative Process Assessment Scale
Prof. Dr. Yvonne Görlich | PFH Private Hochschule Göttingen | Germany
Show details
Author:
Prof. Dr. Yvonne Görlich | PFH Private Hochschule Göttingen | Germany

Der kreative Prozess lässt sich über acht Phasen beschreiben: 1. Problementdeckung, 2. Informationssuche, -aufnahme und -bewertung, 3. Konzeptkombination, 4. Ideenfindung, 5. Entwicklung eines Lösungsansatzes, 6. Ideenbewertung, 7. Anpassung und Umsetzung und 8. Kommunikation und Implementierung. Mit der Creative Process Assessment Scale (CPAS; Görlich, 2023) liegt ein Selbstbeurteilungsinstrument zur Messung dieser Phasen vor. Ziel der vorliegenden Studie war die Validierung der Fremdbeurteilungsversion (CPAS-OR).
905 Personen schätzten den kreativen Prozess einer ihnen bekannten Person ein; von 782 bewerteten Personen lag eine Selbstbeurteilung vor. Zur Validierung wurden die Big Five, Need for Cognition, Lebenszufriedenheit, Risikobereitschaft, Eigeninitiative und Indikatoren kreativer Leistung erhoben.
Cronbachs Alpha betrug für den Gesamtwert .95, die Retest-Reliabilität .85. Konfirmatorische Faktorenanalysen zeigten akzeptable Fit-Indizes für Bifaktor- und hierarchische Modelle bei Kombination der Phasen 4 und 5 zu Kernkreativität. Korrelationsanalysen bestätigten theoretisch vorhergesagte Zusammenhänge: Offenheit korrelierte am stärksten mit Phase 4 (Ideenfindung), Gewissenhaftigkeit mit Phase 7 (Anpassung und Umsetzung) und Extraversion mit Phase 8 (Kommunikation und Implementierung). Need for Cognition korrelierte besonders mit den ersten drei Phasen, Eigeninitiative mit allen Phasen. Die Selbst-Fremd-Übereinstimmung war moderat (r = .43). Kriteriumsvalidität zeigte sich durch positive Zusammenhänge mit Indikatoren kreativer Leistung.
Die CPAS-OR ist ein reliables und valides Instrument zur Messung des kreativen Prozesses aus der Fremdperspektive. Sie eignet sich für organisationale, pädagogische, klinische oder beratungsbezogene Kontexte zur Ergänzung von Selbsteinschätzungen und ermöglicht Multi-Source-Evaluation.

426. Restoring trust in e-commerce: The influence of overcompensation on customer trust
Teresa Anastasia Schmalzl | Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI) | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Teresa Anastasia Schmalzl | Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI) | Germany
Vanessa Gabriela Yarza Narvarro-Schär | Ludwig-Maximilans-Universität München (LMU)
Prof. Dr. Eric Eller | Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI) | Germany
Prof. Dr. Christine Hennighausen | Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt (THI) | Germany

Trust is a key success factor in e-commerce, yet even minor trust violations can severely damage customer relationships. Understanding how trust can be effectively restored is therefore critical for online retail seeking long-term competitiveness and customer loyalty. This study investigates whether overcompensation can rebuild customer trust after a trust violation and whether combining monetary compensation with verbal measures enhances its effectiveness. Using an experimental online design with repeated measurements (mixed 3x5 design), the study examines trust and mistrust before and after a violation, and following different trust recovery strategies. The sample comprised N = 295 participants (M = 25.98 years, 68% female), who evaluated a fashion brand under controlled conditions.
The results demonstrate that overcompensation significantly restores trust after a breach. Importantly, its effectiveness increases when paired with an explanation, highlighting the value of combining monetary and verbal responses. The most comprehensive strategy - overcompensation combined with both explanation and apology - raises trust to a level above the original baseline. However, it does not outperform simpler combinations in a statistically significant way. Due to insufficient scale reliability, hypotheses related to mistrust reduction could not be tested inferentially. These findings provide actionable insights for e-commerce managers by showing that trust recovery does not require maximal effort at all costs. Instead, strategically combining compensation with transparent communication can efficiently rebuild and even strengthen customer trust after a failure.

427. Mindful Up-Skilling? A Meta-Analysis of Mindfulness and Future Skills
Katharina Geppert | EBS University | Germany
Show details
Authors:
Katharina Geppert | EBS University | Germany
Prof. Dr. Myriam Bechtoldt | EBS University of Business and Law

Research on future skills und skill development assumes that transferable skills such as problem solving, collaboration, and critical thinking arise from general psychological processes rather than domain-specific knowledge alone. Mindfulness has been shown to influence both regulatory processes (e.g., attentional and motivational regulation) and cognitive processing (e.g., flexible and elaborative information processing), yet it remains unclear whether these processes relate systematically to competence development. To date, no quantitative synthesis has examined the relationship between mindfulness and future skills.
The present meta-analysis examines whether mindfulness—assessed as both trained and dispositional—is associated with future skills and whether patterns differ across three process-based domains: intrapersonal self-regulation, socio-emotional co-regulation, and cognitive-constructive processing. Because mindfulness targets proximal regulatory processes while influencing higher-order cognition more indirectly, stronger and more consistent associations are expected for self-regulatory competencies, followed by socio-emotional skills, whereas cognitively constructive skills are expected to show more variable associations.
Systematic searches identified 86 eligible articles comprising 235 reported outcomes, with substantially greater coverage of self-regulatory and socio-emotional skills than cognitively constructive competencies. Separate random-effects meta-analyses are conducted for each future skill, and resulting effect patterns are compared across domains. Differences between study types (e.g., intervention vs. cross-sectional) and operationalizations of mindfulness are examined where sufficient data are available.
Screening and coding are complete and statistical analyses are underway. The presentation will report the association patterns between mindfulness and the selected future skills and describe how effects vary across skill domains and study characteristics.

428. Barriers and Drivers: A Comparative Analysis of Women’s Leadership Pathways in STEM and Public Service
Prof. Dr. Petra Kemter-Hofmann | Germany
